title: Fire-protection plan source
description: Woodcore-Datei/fire/<id>.json, schema 2.0 (1.0, whose background is a file only, is read as it is and upgraded on reading -- calc/domains/fire.py `upgrade`) -- one fire-protection plan: the concept of a floor drawn by hand over an architect's plan -- the surfaces of the escape routes, the walls with their fire resistance, the doors, the escape routes' lengths, exits and widths, and a legend. Written by Woodcore's «Plan de protection incendie» tab only, read by calc/domains/fire.py. It either FOLLOWS a position plan (`plan`), whose background, sheet, crop and scale it then takes afresh at every reading, or carries a frame of its own in the very four fields a position plan states (`background`, `sheet`, `crop`, `scale`) -- never both, but for the crop, which a plan that follows may state for itself. Coordinates are in the sheet's units, as a position plan's are: points for a PDF, pixels for an image, from the top left corner with y down. Every id is unique in the plan across all the collections. Every rule the walker below cannot express is checked by fire.check_source.

schema_version.description: -- accepted: 1.0, 2.0 and 2.1; a 1.0 file is read as 2.0, its background being a file only, and written as 2.0 only when it is saved. 2.1 (issue #43) is 2.0 with `texts`, which Woodcore writes only where a text is placed.

id.description: The file name, and the string the report will address the plan by. Letters, digits and _ . + -.

name.description: What the engineer calls this plan, free text (Woodcore's «Nom»). Its ID is composed of it until the ID is written over (calc/tools/identity.py).

label.description: Woodcore's «Description»: free text; may be empty.

group.description: The folder Woodcore files this source in, "" or absent at the root. A field and never a directory (calc/tools/grouped_list.py).

superposition.description: Another plan of the same tab shown over this one in Woodcore's window (v0.116, the «Superposition» module) -- a drawing aid, never printed and never exported: what lies on the storey above or below while this one is drawn. The other plan's point q is shown at s·q + offset, s this plan's units per metre over the other's where both have a scale (else 1). Optional and additive, so schema_version does not move for it; a plan named that no longer exists is shown as nothing, never refused.

plan.description: The id of the plan shown over this one -- a plan of the same tab, never this one.

elements.description: Whether its drawn elements are shown with its background (default true).

opacity.description: How opaque the superposed plan is, 0.05 to 1 (default 0.5).

colour.description: Its background as it is (normal), in grey or in one of five colours (default red).

tint_elements.description: Whether its elements take that colour too (default false: they keep their own).

offset.description: [dx, dy] in this plan's sheet units: where the other plan's origin lands, set by «Aligner» (two clicks). Absent: the two crops' top left corners on each other.

plan.description: The id of the position plan this plan follows (Woodcore-Datei/plans/<id>.json): its background, its sheet and its scale are read from it at every reading, so changing them in «Plan de position» changes them here -- and its crop too, unless this plan states one of its own. Present, neither `background`, `sheet` nor `scale` may be.

background.description: The architect's plan, where this plan has a frame of its own -- a position plan's own field (schemas/plan-source.schema.json): a file of the project, or, since 2.0, a page of a document of plans/documents/ (`document`).

file.description: Its path relative to the project folder, with forward slashes; a .pdf, .png, .jpg or .svg, or a .dxf or .dwg through its document only.

document.description: The document of plans/documents/ the plan is drawn on (calc/domains/plan_documents.py): its file and page are then kept in step with it here, and its rotation and layers are the document's. Optional (2.0): absent, the plan is drawn on `file` directly, as in 1.0.

sheet.description: The size of the sheet, in its units; required where the plan follows no position plan.

crop.description: What the report shows of the sheet. On a plan with a frame of its own, a position plan's own field. On a plan that follows a position plan, the ONE frame field it may state: its own crop, over the position plan's -- absent, the position plan's is taken.

scale.description: How long a metre of the building is on the sheet, as a position plan states it: 'ratio' (1:n) or 'calibration'. The zones are delimited with it -- a door is closed by its width in metres -- and measured with it.

style.description: The plan's own size factors, the position plan's logic (calc/domains/figure_style.py): absent, each is 1. There is no `point`: nothing here is a symbol placed on a point.

line.description: Every stroke, the walls' bands included: from 0.25 to 3.

text.description: Every text of the plan: from 0.25 to 3. The legend has a size of its own.

zones.description: The surfaces: closed outlines drawn by hand, each of one of the three kinds the VKF / AEAI sheet draws as a surface of an escape route.

id.description: Unique in the plan: Z1, Z2, … A number is never given twice, a deleted surface's included.

kind.description: What the surface is: vertical (a vertical escape route), horizontal (a horizontal one) or clear (a surface to be kept clear) -- the keys of calc/norms/vkf-2016-symbole-brandschutzplan.json's `escape`. Absent: a draft, drawn before the kinds existed -- shown in the editor, never printed and in no legend.

label.description: What the engineer calls the surface, free text; may be absent.

points.description: The outline, at least three points, not closed on itself.

holes.description: The islands inside the outline that are not part of the surface, each an outline of its own. No tool draws one today; a file that carries one is read.

style.description: The factors this entry states over the plan's own, each MULTIPLYING it (calc/domains/figure_style.py); absent, it follows the plan. A surface: `line` its outline and hatching, `text` its name.

opacity.description: How opaque the entry is drawn, from 0.1 to 1; absent, its collection's own (fire.OPACITY: a surface is tinted at 0.65, everything else is drawn full).

label_offset.description: How far its text was moved by hand from its own place, [dx, dy] in sheet units; absent, the text stands in its own place. From its own place rather than a point, so that the text follows its entry.

walls.description: The walls with a fire resistance: each a line and one of the classes of the VKF sheet of symbols (calc/norms/vkf-2016-symbole-brandschutzplan.json), drawn as that class's coloured band. Optional and additive: a plan that has none states none.

id.description: Unique in the plan: W1, W2, …

class.description: The fire resistance, by its key: EI 30, EI 60-RF1, REI 60-180, …

points.description: The line, at least two points.

style.description: The factors this entry states over the plan's own, each MULTIPLYING it (calc/domains/figure_style.py); absent, it follows the plan. A wall: `line` the width of its band.

opacity.description: How opaque the entry is drawn, from 0.1 to 1; absent, its collection's own (fire.OPACITY: a surface is tinted at 0.65, everything else is drawn full).

doors.description: The doors, each with the way it opens. Optional and additive.

id.description: Unique in the plan: T1, T2, …

kind.description: swing: a leaf turning on a hinge, drawn as the sheet's quarter disc. slide: a leaf sliding along the wall, drawn as the sheet's flat arrow.

class.description: The door's fire resistance, EI 30 or E 30 -- the two the sheet gives a door --, which fills its symbol with that class's colour. Absent: a door without a fire resistance, drawn in outline; it is no symbol of the sheet.

points.description: Exactly two points. A swing door: its hinge, then the other jamb, which the closed leaf reaches. A sliding door: where the leaf stands closed, then where it slides to.

side.description: 1 or -1: the side of the line from the first point to the second that the door opens to (a swing door) or that its arrowhead rises on (a sliding one). 1 is the side reached by turning that line a quarter towards +y.

style.description: The factors this entry states over the plan's own, each MULTIPLYING it (calc/domains/figure_style.py); absent, it follows the plan. A door: `line` its outline.

opacity.description: How opaque the entry is drawn, from 0.1 to 1; absent, its collection's own (fire.OPACITY: a surface is tinted at 0.65, everything else is drawn full).

routes.description: The escape routes' lengths: each a line from where one stands to the exit, drawn as the sheet's thin green arrow, its head at the last point and its length written along it. Optional and additive.

id.description: Unique in the plan: F1, F2, …

points.description: The line, at least two points; the arrow's head is at the last.

text.description: What is written along the route in place of its measured length; absent or empty, the length is written, where the plan has a scale.

style.description: The factors this entry states over the plan's own, each MULTIPLYING it (calc/domains/figure_style.py); absent, it follows the plan. An escape route's length: `line` its arrow, `text` the length written along it.

opacity.description: How opaque the entry is drawn, from 0.1 to 1; absent, its collection's own (fire.OPACITY: a surface is tinted at 0.65, everything else is drawn full).

label_offset.description: How far its text was moved by hand from its own place, [dx, dy] in sheet units; absent, the text stands in its own place. From its own place rather than a point, so that the text follows its entry.

exits.description: The emergency exits: each the sheet's thick green arrow, from its tail to its tip. Optional and additive.

id.description: Unique in the plan: N1, N2, …

points.description: Exactly two points, the arrow's tail and its tip: its place, its direction and its size.

opacity.description: How opaque the entry is drawn, from 0.1 to 1; absent, its collection's own (fire.OPACITY: a surface is tinted at 0.65, everything else is drawn full).

widths.description: The escape routes' widths: each a green figure written across the passage it measures. Optional and additive.

id.description: Unique in the plan: B1, B2, …

points.description: Exactly two points, one on either side of the passage: the figure is written at their middle, along the line between them.

text.description: What is written in place of the measured width; absent or empty, the width is written to the centimetre, where the plan has a scale.

style.description: The factors this entry states over the plan's own, each MULTIPLYING it (calc/domains/figure_style.py); absent, it follows the plan. A width: `text` its figure.

label_offset.description: How far its text was moved by hand from its own place, [dx, dy] in sheet units; absent, the text stands in its own place. From its own place rather than a point, so that the text follows its entry.

legend.description: The legend drawn on the plan: a box listing every symbol the plan draws (fire.legend_rows). Absent: no legend.

x.description: The box's left edge, in sheet units.

y.description: The box's top edge, in sheet units.

scale.description: The legend's own size factor, from 0.25 to 3; absent, 1.

texts.description: The texts placed with the Text tool (issue #43, calc/domains/figure_text.py): each with an id (X1, X2, …) and centred on its one point. Written only by a source that holds one, whose schema_version says so.

points.description: Its centre on the sheet: one point, as every entry of the plan is moved and turned by its points.

text.description: What is printed, a line per line: `{1}` is a token, where the variable `vars["1"]` is printed; a literal brace is written twice, `{{` and `}}`. A token naming no variable is a defect of the file (D-13). An underscore makes a subscript, as in every label of a figure.

vars.description: The variables the tokens name, by token: a link to a variable of the export, its `show` and its `last` value.

origin.description: 'formulas' for a domain of the «Formules» tab, whose id is `instance`; absent for the export.

show.description: How it is printed (D-09): 'value', its value and unit; 'symbol', its symbol, '=', its value and unit.

last.description: What the variable gave when Woodcore's window last saved (D-14), printed where it can no longer be read, with a warning (D-06).

style.description: The factor this text states over the drawing's: `text` only (figure_style.ENTRY_KEYS).
